previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring a gastrostomy tube and status post bypass reversal was admitted with acute onset of large-volume diarrhea (>9/day), nausea/vomiting with small blood specks after retching, and worsened abdominal pain near the G-tube with poor oral intake. Evaluation showed stable labs and reassuring abdominal exam; abdominal X-ray demonstrated no obstruction or free air. Stool testing was negative for toxigenic C. difficile and positive for norovirus, and she was managed supportively with IV fluids, serial electrolyte monitoring, antiemetics, gastric mucosal protection (IV then oral PPI with ranitidine and sucralfate), and analgesia transitioned from IV morphine to home liquid oxycodone as oral intake improved. Symptoms steadily improved with tolerance of a light bariatric diet (Stage 5) and decreased diarrhea; she was discharged home ambulatory with continuation of home medications, ondansetron as needed, dronabinol held pending outpatient follow-up, and plans for outpatient reassessment of mild proteinuria and bariatric surgery follow-up regarding potential future G-tube removal.

>> ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Norovirus gastroenteritis - Patient was recently discharged 
from the Medicine service with norovirus gastroenteritis. She 
initially presented with similar symptoms as her prior 
admission: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, poor PO intake, and signs 
of dehydration (dry mucous membranes, nondetectable JVP).  Given 
re-presentation with similar symptoms, she was treated for 
likely ongoing viral gastroenteritis with supportive measures. 
SIBO was considered, however given improvement with conservative 
management testing also deferred. She received intravenous 
fluids and electrolytes were monitored closely, which did not 
require repletion.  Her nausea was managed with Zofran 4mg Q8H 
and Compazine 10mg Q6H as needed.  Loperamide was avoided given 
previous exacerbation of her abdominal symptoms.  Her diet was 
slowly advanced from clears to softs to regular diet with Ensure 
supplements with meals.  Her prolonged symptoms of Norovirus may 
be due to her altered GI anatomy from history of RYGB and 
reversal. Given recent diagnosis of Norovirus including C. diff. 
on last admission, stool studies were not repeated. Patient 
evaluated by surgery, stable for discharge, tolerating PO intake 
well without any further episodes of nausea/vomiting. 
.
# Nutrition: Patient was started on a clear liquid diet with 
supplements, and advanced as tolerated. Tube feeds were held 
during this hospitalization due to concern for exacerbating 
diarrheal symptoms.
.
>> CHRONIC ISSUES:
# s/p RYGB reversal: Patient continued to take her home 
Pantoprazole 40mg BID, Ranitidine 150mg QD, and Sucralfate 1gm 
QID for history of marginal ulcers at the gastrojejunal 
anastomosis.  She continued to take her home multivitamin. Her 
home iron 325mg PO was held during this admission to avoid 
contributing to her nausea.
.
# Chronic abdominal pain: Patient continued taking her home 
Gabapentin 600mg TID, Acetaminophen (liquid) 1000mg PO Q8H as 
needed.  Her oxycodone (liquid) ___ Q4H as needed was 
minimized during this hospitalization to avoid contributing to 
abdominal pain
.

Aripiprazole 10mg QD, Fluoxetine 60mg QD, Lorazepam 1mg Q8H as 
needed for anxiety, and Zolpidem 5mg QHS as needed for insomnia.
.
# Hyperlipidemia: Patient continued taking her home Atorvastatin 
40mg QHS.
.
